candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — thermoregulation risk
candidate.educational_objective: Explain key physiologic reasons infants are vulnerable to hypothermia.

options.A: They have immature thermoregulation and a relatively large body surface area in relation to body size.
options.B: They have fully mature temperature regulation and a smaller surface-area-to-mass ratio.
options.C: They generate unlimited heat through shivering immediately after birth.
options.D: They cannot lose heat through evaporation or convection.

candidate.rationale: Young infants have limited thermoregulatory capacity and a relatively large surface-area-to-body-mass relationship, increasing susceptibility to environmental heat loss and hypothermia.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Immature thermoregulation and a large surface-area-to-body-size ratio increase infant hypothermia risk.
candidate.source_locator: Clinical review — infant thermoregulation and high surface-area-to-body-size contribution to heat loss
candidate.stem: Why are young infants particularly vulnerable to hypothermia compared with older children and adults?
